text:
jonathan: quick sync — I ran a speculative-decoding shadow run on the 70B quantized build (q4_k-like profile) with a two-stage prefetch + branch sampler. high-level: ~1.9x tokens/sec speedup overall, p50 latency dropped from ~210ms -> ~115ms. p99 stayed pretty similar (+~6ms).

mei: nice. what was the speculative ratio and fallback policy? any config snippet?

jonathan: config gist below. basically light speculative budget (0.35) and early-accept at top-2 when confidence delta > 0.12. fallback to full decode on low-entropy windows.

```bash
# shadow run command (simplified)
./run_infer --model open-70b-q4 --speculative_budget 0.35 \\n  --early_accept_topk 2 --early_accept_thresh 0.12 \\n  --fallback_policy "entropy:<0.9->full" \ 
  --batch 8 --seq_len 1024 --shadow true
```

alex: can you paste the eval numbers vs baseline on our holdout? percent-deltas are easiest.

jonathan: sure — small table from the automated eval (1k prompts, held-out instruction set):

- exact-match: baseline 42.8% -> spec 42.1% (-0.7 pts)
- rouge-L: baseline 61.2 -> spec 60.9 (-0.3)
- ppl (1k tok): baseline 12.4 -> spec 12.6 (+0.2)
- latency p50: 210ms -> 115ms (-45%)
- latency p99: 980ms -> 986ms (+0.6%)
- tokens/sec: 720 -> 1370 (+90%)

mei: that EM drop is small but non-negligible. where are the regressions concentrated? long-generation vs short?

jonathan: mostly long code completions and multi-step math. a few hallucinations where speculative path accepted a token sequence that later forced low-quality continuation. short Q&A and summarization unchanged.

sara: do we have per-prompt examples for the worst regressions? want to check pattern (beam collapse vs truncated prefix).

jonathan: uploaded 12 worst failures to the artifact bucket: s3://redwood-shadow/artifacts/1789991111/worst-12.jsonl — includes model logits and the speculative accept flags.

alex: can eval-bot post a quick diff for the top 5 failure cases (diff between baseline and spec)?

eval-bot: auto-report: generated diffs for top-5 by EM delta and attached gist: https://internal.gists/rw/1789991111-diffs

mei: thanks. next steps IMHO:
- run 10k shadow queries with same config but vary speculative_budget in {0.2,0.35,0.5}
- add a confidence smoothing window (len=3) before early-accept to reduce one-off noisy accepts
- run targeted long-code holdout (n=500) as a canary to catch regressions faster

sara: +1. Also let's re-run with temperature 0.7/1.0 to see sampling effects — speculative might overcommit at higher temps.

jonathan: assigning: i'll run the budget sweep and long-code canary by EOD tomorrow. alex, can you wire up the smoothing change into the runtime (small patch) and run a short 1k test?

alex: on it. patch will be trivial — add exponential smoothing on token-confidence. will push branch `spec-smooth-1789` and link the PR here.

jonathan: FYI we also toggled quantization micro-optim: switched kernel pack from blocksize 32->16 to reduce quant noise slightly. marginal improvement on ppl (~0.05).

mei: cool — keep an eye on memory overhead for smaller blocksize. does the runtime fallback still fit in our Dedicated pools?

jonathan: yes, memory+GPU util within limits on our test rig (A100-80G), but need to revalidate on 40G nodes.

sara: if the sweep shows the EM hit goes away at budget 0.2 with most of speedup preserved, we can promote a canary rollout in prod-dedicated for a subset of routes (low-code, short-exec).

jonathan: agreed. plan: run sweep, post full 10k metrics, then decide. will tag folks back here. thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:

alex: PR: https://git.internal/rw/spec-smooth-1789 — running test now.

eval-bot: shadow-run summary uploaded: s3://redwood-shadow/1789991111/summary.json — contains full metrics, per-route breakdown, and artifacts.

jonathan: cool — will close loop tomorrow. if anyone wants to look at the failure set earlier ping me and I'll share credentials.

mei: sounds good.

sara: thanks all.
